title: Family History
note: Only facts confirmed with Ann (or strongly supported public military/civil records she accepted) are marked confirmed. Sources are public web records.

sections.title: Otto J. Krause — WWII B-17 navigator
sections.summary: Otto J. Krause of Detroit served as a navigator with the 91st Bomb Group, 324th Bomb Squadron, Eighth Air Force, based at RAF Bassingbourn. He flew mostly on B-17 Mah Ideel (43-37993 DF-N) with Lt. William Laws’ crew, earned the Air Medal with oak leaf clusters, and finished as a First Lieutenant. He married Geraldine Staub around 1945.
highlights: Unit: 91st Bomb Group / 324th BS / 8th Air Force
Aircraft: Mah Ideel (serial 43-37993, DF-N), ~72 missions; returned to the U.S. June 1945
Crew: Lt. William V. Laws (pilot); co-pilot Bernard “Ed” Goldstein was KIA 30 Nov 1944 while flying with another crew
Awards: Air Medal + oak leaf clusters (orders in late 1944)
Wartime photo FRE 5634 by Dale Darling shows Otto with a B-17

sections.title: Jerome Frederick Crosier & Madeline Phoebe Lozon
sections.summary: Jerome Frederick Crosier (31 Jan 1898, Lansing, MI – 28 Oct 1983, Avon, MI), son of Albert David Crosier and Marion A. Maher, married Madeline Phoebe Lozon on 25 Nov 1924 in Wallaceburg, Ontario. Madeline (b. 9 Feb 1894, Wallaceburg) died 29 Sep 1925 in Detroit — the same day their son Frederick Charles was born. Jerome later remarried Josephine C. (c. 1905–1997), who raised Frederick as his stepmother.
highlights: Marriage: 25 Nov 1924, Wallaceburg, Ontario
Madeline died 29 Sep 1925 in Detroit, the day Frederick was born
Stepmother: Josephine C. Crosier (c. 1905–1997)
Jerome’s parents: Albert David Crosier (1865–1942) & Marion A. Maher (1865–1951)
Jerome birth/death: 31 Jan 1898 Lansing – 28 Oct 1983 Avon, MI

sections.title: Adolphus Lozon & Mary Veronica Gore
sections.summary: Madeline’s parents were Adolphus Lozon (b. ~1861) and Mary Veronica Gore (b. ~1863) of the Wallaceburg / Chatham, Ontario area. They married 8 Jan 1883. Known children include Madeline Phoebe, Peter Adolphus, Aubrey Samuel, Roy Clarence, Wilfred Joseph, and an infant who died in 1903. Canadian service records also list Solomon Alex Lozon (b. 6 Nov 1891, Wallaceburg) as a son of Adolphus.
highlights: Married 8 Jan 1883
Home area: Wallaceburg / Chatham, Kent County, Ontario
Children include Madeline, Peter, Aubrey, Roy, Wilfred, Solomon Alex

sections.title: Lozon brothers — WWI Canadian service
sections.summary: Two of Madeline’s brothers appear in Canadian WWI records from Wallaceburg. Solomon Alex Lozon (sapper #3131895) enlisted Feb 1918 with the 1st Western Ontario Regiment, sailed to England May 1918, and served in France before returning in 1919. Peter Adolphus (Dulphy) Lozon (#3134471), born 29 Aug 1896, enlisted July 1918 and was discharged early 1919.
highlights: Solomon Alex Lozon — Spr., CEF 3131895; overseas England/France 1918–19
Peter Adolphus Lozon — 1st WOR 3134471; enlisted 1918, demobilized 1919
Both listed with Adolphus/Mary Lozon of R.R. #2 Wallaceburg area
